opening_message:
Ticket 1: Traci Lowe (employee ID E041) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E041.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst. Admin on Source Code is only allowed when the employee's role owns the system (Engineer). Since the requested admin exceeds the maximum for a full-time Analyst, I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E041 (Traci Lowe) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors are never admin; write requires advanced training. Requested admin exceeds max of read, so recommend granting read.
reason: The notes conflict on Traci Lowe's (E041) employment type: HR reports full-time Analyst (max write on Source Code, since admin requires the Engineer role), while Security reports contractor with basic training (max read, and contractors are never admin). Since the employment-type fact is pivotal and disputed, I apply least privilege. Requested admin exceeds the maximum under both interpretations, and read is within the limit under either, so granting read is the safe maximum.
